headline: Kanlaon Records Ash Emission as PHIVOLCS Maintains Alert Level 2
seoTitle: Kanlaon Ash Emission Recorded; Alert Level 2 Maintained | FMB News
seoDescription: PHIVOLCS recorded an ash emission event at Kanlaon Volcano early August 20 while maintaining Alert Level 2 and the four-kilometer permanent danger zone.
deck: PHIVOLCS kept Kanlaon at Alert Level 2 after an early-morning ash emission and reiterated restrictions around the permanent danger zone.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PHIVOLCS recorded an ash emission event at Kanlaon Volcano at about 5:24 AM on Thursday, August 20, according to the approved FMB News morning package.
Alert Level 2 remained in effect, indicating increased volcanic unrest, while the four-kilometer Permanent Danger Zone remained restricted.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Kanlaon is an active volcano on Negros Island and is closely monitored for changes in gas emission, seismic activity, ash events and other signs of unrest.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Ash emissions can affect nearby communities and aviation depending on wind direction and plume height. Entry into the Permanent Danger Zone is restricted because sudden steam-driven or phreatic activity can occur during periods of unrest.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Residents, local governments and aviation operators should follow PHIVOLCS bulletins for any change in alert level, ashfall advisories, volcanic earthquakes or stronger emissions.
